questions.prompt: In **Logic Programming** (e.g., Prolog), what are the two main components of a program? (Select all that apply.)
What is **unification** in Prolog?

options.text: Compiling multiple files into one binary
Bidirectional pattern matching that binds logic variables so two terms become identical

questions.prompt: How does **Datalog** differ from full Prolog?

options.text: Datalog allows arbitrary side effects and cuts
Datalog is only for UI rendering
Datalog restricts terms to flat constants/variables (no arbitrary nested function symbols) so recursive queries always terminate in polynomial time

questions.prompt: What problem class does **Clingo (Answer Set Programming)** target?

options.text: Declarative combinatorial search, scheduling, and constraint satisfaction via stable models

questions.prompt: What does **Mercury** add to Prolog-style logic programming?

options.text: Strong static types, explicit argument modes (`in`/`out`), and determinism declarations checked at compile time

questions.prompt: Match each logic-programming tool/language to its focus.

columns.label: General SLD resolution with backtracking & cuts
Terminating recursive queries over relational facts
Combinatorial constraint solving via stable models

questions.prompt: What problem does **Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP)** address?

options.text: Separating **cross-cutting concerns** (logging, auth, transactions, metrics) from core business logic

questions.prompt: Select the three core vocabulary terms in AspectJ / AOP. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Advice (code executed before, after, or around a join point)
Join point (execution point such as a method call)

questions.prompt: How do **AspectJ** and **PostSharp** typically differ from **Spring AOP**?

options.text: AspectJ/PostSharp support compile-time or load-time bytecode/IL weaving, whereas Spring AOP uses runtime dynamic proxies

questions.prompt: What defines **Component-Oriented Programming**?

options.text: Assembling systems from self-contained, replaceable units that communicate strictly through explicit interfaces/contracts

questions.prompt: Select the three browser standards that make up native **Web Components**. (Select all that apply.)
What problem does **OSGi** solve on the Java platform?

options.text: Dynamic module lifecycle (install, start, stop, update) with explicit package import/export versioning

questions.prompt: In **Concurrent & Actor Programming** (Erlang, Elixir, Pony), how do actors avoid shared-memory data races?

options.text: By locking a single global mutex
Each actor owns isolated private state and communicates solely via asynchronous message passing

questions.prompt: What is the **'Let it crash'** philosophy in Erlang/Elixir supervision trees?

options.text: Exit the entire OS process on any error
Isolate failures inside lightweight processes and let a Supervisor restart failed workers to a clean known state

questions.prompt: How does **Go's CSP model** (Communicating Sequential Processes) differ from the Actor model?

options.text: Goroutines are anonymous and communicate through explicit, typed **channels** (often synchronous rendezvous)
Go processes are named actors with mailboxes

questions.prompt: How does **Pony** guarantee data-race freedom at compile time without a garbage-collector stop-the-world pause across actors?

options.text: Using **reference capabilities** (`iso`, `val`, `ref`, `box`, `trn`, `tag`) checked by the compiler
By copying every byte on every line

questions.prompt: What defines **Reactive & Dataflow Programming**?

options.text: Computation is modeled as propagation of changes through streams or dependency graphs
Data is stored only on tape

questions.prompt: In **RxJS**, what is the difference between an `Observable` and a plain `Promise`?

options.text: An `Observable` is lazy (starts on `subscribe`) and can emit 0..N values over time with cancellation (`unsubscribe`); a `Promise` is eager and resolves once

code.source:
clicks = (x for x in [1, 2, 3])
doubled = map(lambda v: v * 2, clicks)

questions.prompt: What are the three core parts of **The Elm Architecture (TEA)**?

options.text: **Model** (state), **Update** (pure state transition on `Msg`), and **View** (pure `Model -> Html Msg`)

questions.prompt: How is a program represented in **LabVIEW** (visual dataflow)?

options.text: Block diagrams where nodes execute as soon as all their input wires have data

questions.prompt: What defines **Array-Oriented Programming** (APL, J, BQN)?

options.text: Whole-array operations, automatic rank/broadcasting, and tacit (point-free) function composition

questions.prompt: What does **tacit (point-free) programming** in J or BQN mean?

options.text: Defining functions by composing operators/verbs without naming explicit argument variables

code.source:
avg = lambda xs: sum(xs) / len(xs)
# tacit in J: +/ % #

questions.prompt: In **Angular** and **.NET Components**, what role does **Dependency Injection (DI)** play?

options.text: It decouples components from concrete service instantiation, improving testability and modularity

questions.prompt: What is **backtracking** in Prolog or constraint solvers?

options.text: Rewinding to the most recent choice point when a branch fails and trying the next alternative

questions.prompt: What does **Shadow DOM** provide for Web Components?

options.text: Scoped DOM and CSS encapsulation so component styles do not leak out or collide with page styles

questions.prompt: What is a **pure** RxJS operator like `switchMap` used for in search-as-you-type UIs?

options.text: Cancelling the previous in-flight inner observable whenever a new input arrives, preventing stale responses

questions.prompt: Why do **Elixir** and **Erlang** spawn hundreds of thousands of processes on a single machine?

options.text: They use no memory at all
BEAM processes are lightweight user-space tasks (~few KB heap, preemptive reductions) rather than OS threads
They run on separate physical machines automatically

questions.prompt: What is a major risk of overusing **Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP)**?

options.text: Hidden control flow ('spooky action at a distance') where reading a method no longer reveals intercepted behavior
Loss of strong typing in SQL

questions.prompt: Select all accurate comparisons between **Array Programming** and explicit `for` loops. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Array expressions enable SIMD/vectorized execution in native runtimes
Rank/broadcasting rules eliminate nested loop indexing errors
Succinct expressions can compress dense math into a single line

options.text: A decorator wrapping a function to add cross-cutting logging (an AOP-like pattern)

questions.prompt: In **CSP (Go)**, what happens when two goroutines meet on an unbuffered channel `ch <- v` and `<-ch`?

options.text: Both synchronize (rendezvous) until the value is handed off directly

questions.prompt: What is **broadcasting** (rank polymorphism) in array-oriented languages like APL/BQN or NumPy?

options.text: Sending UDP packets to all hosts
Automatically stretching a scalar or lower-rank array along matching axes to match a higher-rank operand

shifted = [[x + 1 for x in row] for row in matrix]

questions.prompt: Why does **Elm** claim 'no runtime exceptions in practice'?

options.text: Strict static types, algebraic `Maybe`/`Result` instead of `null`/exceptions, and pure functions catch missing cases at compile time

questions.prompt: In **Prolog**, what does the cut operator (`!`) do?

options.text: Commits to choices made so far in the current clause, pruning backtracking

questions.prompt: What makes **LabVIEW**'s dataflow naturally parallel?

options.text: Two independent branches with no data dependency between them can execute concurrently without explicit threads

What does `customElements.define('user-card', UserCard)` do in Web Components?

options.text: Registers a reusable HTML tag backed by a class extending `HTMLElement`

questions.prompt: In **Erlang/Elixir**, what is a **Supervision Tree**?

options.text: A hierarchy of supervisor and worker processes defining restart strategies (`one_for_one`, `one_for_all`, `rest_for_one`) on crash
